claims.text: Replacing a portion of Hf and Mo in as-cast HfMoTaTiZr with Sc or Y will reduce alloy density.
Sc or Y substitution can reduce density without significantly compromising room-temperature mechanical performance.
Sc or Y substitution can reduce density without significantly compromising high-temperature mechanical performance.
Introducing Sc or Y in place of Hf and Mo will reduce the alloy's average atomic mass.
Reducing the average atomic mass through the proposed substitution will decrease alloy density.
Sc or Y has a smaller atomic radius than Hf or Mo.
Sc or Y substitution may enhance grain-boundary cohesion.
Sc or Y substitution may reduce lattice distortion.
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion and reduced lattice distortion may preserve alloy strength.
The proposed substitution can reduce density by at least 5%.
The modified alloy can retain a room-temperature yield strength above 1500 MPa under uniaxial tensile loading.
The modified alloy can retain a yield strength above 800 MPa at 1000 °C under uniaxial tensile loading.
The proposed substitution will cause only a minimal decrease in fracture toughness.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of about 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of 855 MPa.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis states that the substitution amount requires optimization, implying that some tested variants may fail while an optimized variant may succeed. The rejection rule instead declares the hypothesis falsified if any variant achieving the density target fails either strength threshold.
